anomalies.observed: The CAN BUS section contains a third MCP2515-xSO CAN controller U10, in addition to U8 and U9. U10 is wired with SPI signals (CAN1_CIPO, CAN1_COPI, CAN1_CS1, CAN1_SCK) and has the full MCP2515 pinout. The isolated CAN transceiver that should accompany U9 for CAN1 is not present; only U11 (for CAN0) is drawn.
anomalies.expected: The specification calls for exactly two isolated CAN buses, each driven by its own MCP2515 controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion). Only two MCP2515 controllers and two isolated transceivers should exist.

evidence.quote: U10 MCP2515-xSO ... CAN1_CIPO, CAN1_COPI, CAN1_CS1, CAN1_SCK (CAN BUS section, image 9)
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The extra U10 controller may contend on the CAN1 SPI bus or be non-functional. More critically, CAN1 has no isolated transceiver, so it cannot drive or receive the physical CAN1 bus, making CAN1 inoperable.

anomalies.observed: U6 (LTC4412xS6) has its VIN pin 5 connected to net VBUS_5V_ENA and its SENSE pin 4 connected to net VBUS_5V_IN. The USB input from the USB-C connector is USBC_VBUS_IN/VBUS_5V_IN, while VBUS_5V_ENA is the switched output side.
anomalies.expected: For an ideal-diode controller, VIN must connect to the input supply (USB VBUS, i.e. VBUS_5V_IN/USBC_VBUS_IN) and SENSE must connect to the output (VBUS_5V_ENA).

evidence.quote: U6 LTC4412xS6: pin 5 VIN -> VBUS_5V_ENA; pin 4 SENSE -> VBUS_5V_IN (USB section, image 2)
U6 — LTC4412xS6 ... USB power-path controller intended to OR/protect a USB power input

anomalies.impact: The ideal-diode control loop is reversed. It will not conduct correctly from the USB input to the system rail; it may block USB power entirely or allow reverse current, defeating the intended ORing and reverse-current protection.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains two significant deviations from the intended design: an extra MCP2515 CAN controller (U10) with a missing CAN1 isolated transceiver, and swapped VIN/SENSE connections on the LTC4412 ideal-diode controller U6. Both would prevent the board from behaving as specified.
